page: Microsoft Azure E32-8as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained-core architecture. Powered by the AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 256.0 GB of system memory, delivering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per core. The configuration includes 550 GB of local temporary SSD storage and operates without bundled GPU hardware, managed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks reflect strong single-threaded CPU capabilities alongside stable, mid-tier multi-threaded execution. In stress testing, single-core processing rated in the upper quartile, while multi-core metrics and Geekbench results (1607 single-core, 6370 multi-core) aligned with standard 8-vCPU expectations. Uncached memory read bandwidth measured 39.69 GB/sec, whereas uncached write bandwidth registered at 23.0 GB/sec, representing a lower-tier result. In-memory throughput reached 8.08 million Redis SET operations per second, with PassMark database operations scoring 3289.56.

The primary efficiency tradeoff of the E32-8as_v4 stems from its constrained vCPU model. By pairing 256 GB of memory with only 8 active cores instead of the full 32 cores typical of the host chassis, it significantly reduces per-core software licensing expenses for database engines that require massive RAM footprints but limited compute parallelism. Conversely, tasks constrained by uncached memory write throughput or large-scale multi-threaded compilation will find fewer performance advantages.

This server type is primarily suited for large-footprint relational database engines such as SQL Server and Oracle, enterprise caching layers, and in-memory analytical workloads where memory capacity is the primary constraint rather than core count.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive workloads requiring reduced CPU core counts. Based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and an expansive 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding 32 GB per vCPU. The instance is bundled with 550 GB of local SSD storage and features no GPU acceleration. Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU throughput alongside average multi-core and database transaction performance, with Redis achieving 8.08 million operations per second. However, uncached memory write bandwidth is comparatively limited at 23.0 GB/sec. The instance delivers notable licensing cost efficiency for software billed per core, making it well suited for enterprise database management systems, in-memory caching tiers, and memory-bound transactional applications.
